value: MEASUREMENT-SCOPE LAW, and a REFUTATION of a standing deletion list. fndiff/regnorm/objdiff all score the FINAL, WEBFRANK-POSTPROCESSED object, not the compiler's output. Therefore ANY function carrying a WebFrank pin measures `real 0` by construction, and a 'has this park become stale?' screen built on fndiff --count is circular: it cannot distinguish a genuinely solved function from one whose residual is merely being rewritten by a sanctioned postprocessor rule. CONCRETE REFUTATION: claim.regnorm-park-label-census-legacy-blanket-corpus.20260831.v1 published a 32-id STALE-SOLVED deletion list (attempt.parked.{allocmem32,atreeinitsub,audioang,audioplayereatsfx,critterlinenodecolsub,critterlookforcriticalmove,dmgfxadd,g3dupdatepadstatus,initanim,initlighting,mbnewfont,missilecollideenemy,pointlinedist2d,fn_800920e0,adjust_radius_8002b2d4,closest_enemy,dbgtextinit,fn_800511d0,fn_800b27c4,fn_800c031c,fn_800c1004,fn_800d967c,fn_800da6a4,gendir_8004fbc8,getsincos,joyreadpad,move_logic00,move_logic02,move_logic04,move_logic30,sndvoiceupdateall,vsprintf}.20260829.v1) and stated that only 'several' were WebFrank-pinned, naming 7. MEASURED TRUTH: ALL 32 ARE PINNED (32/32 present in config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json with before_sha256/after_sha256 and 'Pure allocator recolor' mechanisms). 28 of the 32 park records ALREADY CARRY the explicit attribute postprocessor_covered = 'function reaches 100% only via the guarded postprocessor rule; the source-level allocator wall this park describes still exists' — i.e. the records stated in plain language that they were not stale, and the census listed them for deletion anyway. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: `gdlmem.py stale` reports stale_solved = 0 and places all 32 in postprocessor_walls (41 entries), whose own note reads 'postprocessor_walls are valid source-level walls'. CONSEQUENCE: ZERO of the 32 were deleted; deleting them would have destroyed the only record of 32 live source-level walls while leaving their frozen pinned sources in place (AGENTS.md trap 4: a pinned function's source is hash-asserted and FROZEN, so the wall can never be rediscovered by editing). STANDING RULE: a park is stale-solved ONLY if the function measures real 0 AND carries no WebFrank/P6Frank pin. The correct screen is `gdlmem.py stale`'s stale_solved bucket (which already applies this test), never a raw fndiff sweep. Corollary for the whole project: fndiff `real 0` answers 'does the shipped object match?', not 'is the source solved?' — for any question about SOURCE progress, subtract the pinned set first. The census's own headline metric (blanket labels correct 1-in-156) is unaffected and stands; only its deletion list is withdrawn.
